26648	    def _validate_min_hit_rate_drop(
26649	        min_hit_rate_drop: Any,
26650	    ) -> tuple[int, int]:
26651	        """Validate the minimum hit-rate drop threshold.
26652	
26653	        Used only by
26654	        :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regressions`,
26655	        before any state lookup: ``min_hit_rate_drop`` must be a tuple
26656	        (else :class:`TypeError`) of exactly two non-``bool``
26657	        :class:`int` values (a ``bool`` or non-:class:`int` element
26658	        raises :class:`TypeError`); a wrong element count, a negative
26659	        numerator, a non-positive denominator or a numerator exceeding
26660	        the denominator raises :class:`ValueError`.
26661	        """
26662	        if not isinstance(min_hit_rate_drop, tuple):
26663	            raise TypeError(
26664	                f"min_hit_rate_drop must be a tuple, got "
26665	                f"{type(min_hit_rate_drop).__name__}"
26666	            )
26667	        if len(min_hit_rate_drop) != 2:
26668	            raise ValueError(
26669	                f"min_hit_rate_drop must have exactly 2 elements, got "
26670	                f"{len(min_hit_rate_drop)}"
26671	            )
26672	        numerator, denominator = min_hit_rate_drop
26673	        for position, part in enumerate(min_hit_rate_drop):
26674	            name = f"min_hit_rate_drop[{position}]"
26675	            if isinstance(part, bool) or not isinstance(part, int):
26676	                raise TypeError(
26677	                    f"{name} must be an int, got {type(part).__name__}"
26678	                )
26679	        if numerator < 0:
26680	            raise ValueError(
26681	                "min_hit_rate_drop numerator must be non-negative"
26682	            )
26683	        if denominator < 1:
26684	            raise ValueError(
26685	                "min_hit_rate_drop denominator must be positive"
26686	            )
26687	        if numerator > denominator:
26688	            raise ValueError(
26689	                "min_hit_rate_drop numerator must not exceed the "
26690	                "denominator"
26691	            )
26692	        return (numerator, denominator)

26712	                f"{type(split_cutoffs).__name__}"
26713	            )

26717	            name = f"split_cutoffs[{position}]"
26718	            if isinstance(split_cutoff, bool) or not isinstance(

26723	                    f"{type(split_cutoff).__name__}"

        """Project each steady regression-wave cadence past the last wave.

        stage cap, wave construction, recurrence aggregation,

        membership check and any state lookup), keeping the same

        :class:`int` values of at least one (a ``bool`` or

        wave periodicity query: the one frozen view produces exactly
        the complete periodicity record set a regression wave
        periodicities call with the same arguments would return, with
        every underlying stage cap and every underlying exception
        unchanged. The serial number of the last regression wave in
        that wave set is the observation boundary. For each
        periodicity record, candidate waves start at the record's own
        ``last_wave`` and advance by its median ``period`` one ordinal
        at a time; a candidate is kept only when strictly greater than
        the boundary and at most the boundary plus
        ``regression_wave_horizon``, so the range is never truncated
        and no prediction is ever represented as an observed wave.

        ``forecasts, totals``. Each kept record is a fresh dict
        reproducing every periodicity field in the same order --
        ``identity, waves, first_wave, last_wave, span, points,
        peak_active, appearances, intervals, period, jitter`` -- and
        appending a ``forecasts`` tuple in ascending ordinal order;
        each prediction is a fresh dict with keys ordered ``ordinal,

        candidate in range is dropped; the kept records preserve the

    @staticmethod
    def _validate_min_hit_rate_drop(
        min_hit_rate_drop: Any,
    ) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Validate the minimum hit-rate drop threshold.

        Used only by
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regressions`,
        before any state lookup: ``min_hit_rate_drop`` must be a tuple
        (else :class:`TypeError`) of exactly two non-``bool``
        :class:`int` values (a ``bool`` or non-:class:`int` element
        raises :class:`TypeError`); a wrong element count, a negative
        numerator, a non-positive denominator or a numerator exceeding
        the denominator raises :class:`ValueError`.
        """
        if not isinstance(min_hit_rate_drop, tuple):
            raise TypeError(
                f"min_hit_rate_drop must be a tuple, got "
                f"{type(min_hit_rate_drop).__name__}"
            )
        if len(min_hit_rate_drop) != 2:
            raise ValueError(
                f"min_hit_rate_drop must have exactly 2 elements, got "
                f"{len(min_hit_rate_drop)}"
            )
        numerator, denominator = min_hit_rate_drop
        for position, part in enumerate(min_hit_rate_drop):
            name = f"min_hit_rate_drop[{position}]"
            if isinstance(part, bool) or not isinstance(part, int):
                raise TypeError(
                    f"{name} must be an int, got {type(part).__name__}"
                )
        if numerator < 0:
            raise ValueError(
                "min_hit_rate_drop numerator must be non-negative"
            )
        if denominator < 1:
            raise ValueError(
                "min_hit_rate_drop denominator must be positive"
            )
        if numerator > denominator:
            raise ValueError(
                "min_hit_rate_drop numerator must not exceed the "
                "denominator"
            )
        return (numerator, denominator)

    @staticmethod
    def _validate_drift_scan_split_cutoffs(
        split_cutoffs: Any,
    ) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        """Validate the scan split tuple's types and strict ordering.

        Used only by :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_scan`, before
        any state lookup: ``split_cutoffs`` must be a tuple (else
        :class:`TypeError`) of non-``bool`` :class:`int` values (a
        ``bool`` or non-:class:`int` element raises
        :class:`TypeError`); a duplicate or non-strictly-increasing
        element raises :class:`ValueError`. An empty tuple is legal.
        Membership in the requested cutoffs is settled by
        :meth:`_validate_drift_scan_splits`.
        """
        if not isinstance(split_cutoffs, tuple):
            raise TypeError(
                f"split_cutoffs must be a tuple, got "
                f"{type(split_cutoffs).__name__}"
            )
        validated: list[int] = []
        previous: int | None = None
        for position, split_cutoff in enumerate(split_cutoffs):
            name = f"split_cutoffs[{position}]"
            if isinstance(split_cutoff, bool) or not isinstance(
                split_cutoff, int
            ):
                raise TypeError(
                    f"{name} must be an int, got "
                    f"{type(split_cutoff).__name__}"
                )
            if previous is not None and split_cutoff <= previous:
                raise ValueError(
                    "split_cutoffs must be strictly increasing"
                )
            previous = split_cutoff
            validated.append(split_cutoff)
        return tuple(validated)

    def _validate_drift_scan_splits(

                    f"split_cutoff {split_cutoff} is not one of the "
                    f"requested cutoffs"

                raise ValueError(
                    f"split_cutoff {split_cutoff} leaves an empty baseline "
                    f"or recent period"

def _build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_forecasts_result(
        periodicity_records: tuple[dict[str, object], ...],
        boundary: int,
        regression_wave_horizon: int,
        regression_wave_forecast_limit: int,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Project each steady regression-wave cadence past the boundary.

        Used only by
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_forecasts`.
        The records are the complete, already-bounded and
        already-sorted ``periodicities`` tuple of
        :meth:`_build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_periodicities_result`,
        and ``boundary`` is the serial number of the last regression
        wave in the wave set (``-1`` when no regression wave
        qualified). For each record, candidate waves start at the
        record's own ``last_wave`` and advance by its median
        ``period`` one ordinal at a time; a candidate is kept only
        when strictly greater than ``boundary`` and at most
        ``boundary + regression_wave_horizon``, so the range is never
        truncated. Each prediction is a fresh ``ordinal, wave,
        earliest, latest`` dict: ``ordinal`` is the one-based order
        after the identity's last appearance, ``wave`` is
        ``last_wave + ordinal * period`` and ``earliest``/``latest``
        are ``last_wave + ordinal * min(intervals)`` and
        ``last_wave + ordinal * max(intervals)``.

        A record with no candidate in range is dropped; every kept
        record is a fresh copy of the periodicity record with every
        field in the same order and an appended ascending-ordinal
        ``forecasts`` tuple, keeping the periodicity sort order. The
        complete prediction set is built before the
        ``regression_wave_forecast_limit`` cap -- measured across
        every prediction, not every identity -- is enforced, so an
        over-limit query raises :class:`ValueError` without returning
        partial records. ``totals`` is a fresh dict ordered
        ``identities, predictions, waves, points, first_wave,
        last_wave`` holding the kept-identity count, the summed
        prediction count, the summed participating-wave count, the
        summed point count and the earliest and latest participating
        wave numbers (six zeros when nothing projects); no prediction
        is ever represented as an observed wave. Every record,
        appearance and prediction dict is built fresh and shares no
        mutable object with the periodicity records.
        """
        upper = boundary + regression_wave_horizon
        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        prediction_count = 0
        total_waves = 0
        total_points = 0
        for record in periodicity_records:
            last_wave = record["last_wave"]
            period = record["period"]
            intervals = record["intervals"]
            smallest = min(intervals)
            largest = max(intervals)

            forecasts: list[dict[str, object]] = []
            ordinal = 1
            while True:
                wave = last_wave + ordinal * period
                if wave > upper:
                    break
                if wave > boundary:
                    forecasts.append(
                        {
                            "ordinal": ordinal,
                            "wave": wave,
                            "earliest": last_wave + ordinal * smallest,
                            "latest": last_wave + ordinal * largest,
                        }
                    )
                ordinal += 1
            if not forecasts:
                continue

            records.append(
                {
                    "identity": BranchStore._freeze_lifetime_value(
                        record["identity"]
                    ),
                    "waves": record["waves"],
                    "first_wave": record["first_wave"],
                    "last_wave": last_wave,
                    "span": record["span"],
                    "points": record["points"],
                    "peak_active": record["peak_active"],
                    "appearances": tuple(
                        dict(appearance)
                        for appearance in record["appearances"]
                    ),
                    "intervals": tuple(
                        interval for interval in intervals
                    ),
                    "period": period,
                    "jitter": record["jitter"],
                    "forecasts": tuple(forecasts),
                }
            )
            prediction_count += len(forecasts)
            total_waves += record["waves"]
            total_points += record["points"]

        if prediction_count > regression_wave_forecast_limit:
            raise ValueError(
                f"lifetime churn drift wave prediction scorecard "
                f"regression wave forecast limit exceeded: "
                f"{prediction_count} prediction records, limit is "
                f"{regression_wave_forecast_limit}"
            )

        totals = {
            "identities": len(records),
            "predictions": prediction_count,
            "waves": total_waves,
            "points": total_points,
            "first_wave": 0,
            "last_wave": 0,
        }
        if records:
            totals["first_wave"] = min(
                record["first_wave"] for record in records
            )
            totals["last_wave"] = max(
                record["last_wave"] for record in records
            )
        return {"forecasts": tuple(records), "totals": totals}

    @staticmethod
    def _validate_wave_cutoffs(wave_cutoffs: Any) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        """Validate the wave cutoff tuple's types, signs and ordering.

        Used only by
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_backtests`,
        before any state lookup: ``wave_cutoffs`` must be a tuple (else
        :class:`TypeError`) of non-``bool`` :class:`int` values (a
        ``bool`` or non-:class:`int` element raises
        :class:`TypeError`); a negative, duplicate or
        non-strictly-increasing element raises :class:`ValueError`.
        Range against the actual drift wave count is the caller's
        concern, since the wave set is only known after the frozen
        view is captured.
        """
        if not isinstance(wave_cutoffs, tuple):
            raise TypeError(
                f"wave_cutoffs must be a tuple, got "
                f"{type(wave_cutoffs).__name__}"
            )
        validated: list[int] = []
        previous: int | None = None
        for position, wave_cutoff in enumerate(wave_cutoffs):
            name = f"wave_cutoffs[{position}]"
            if isinstance(wave_cutoff, bool) or not isinstance(
                wave_cutoff, int
            ):
                raise TypeError(
                    f"{name} must be an int, got "
                    f"{type(wave_cutoff).__name__}"
                )
            if wave_cutoff < 0:
                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be non-negative")
            if previous is not None and wave_cutoff <= previous:
                raise ValueError(
                    "wave_cutoffs must be strictly increasing"
                )
            previous = wave_cutoff
            validated.append(wave_cutoff)
        return tuple(validated)

    @staticmethod
    def _validate_backtest_cutoffs(cutoffs: Any) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        """Validate the cutoff tuple's types, non-negativity and ordering.

        Used only by :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_backtests`, before
        any state lookup: ``cutoffs`` must be a tuple (else
        :class:`TypeError`) of non-``bool`` :class:`int` values (a
        ``bool`` or non-:class:`int` element raises :class:`TypeError`);
        a negative, duplicate or non-strictly-increasing element raises
        :class:`ValueError`. Range against the actual wave count is the
        caller's concern, since the wave set is only known after the
        frozen view is captured.
        """
        if not isinstance(cutoffs, tuple):
            raise TypeError(
                f"cutoffs must be a tuple, got {type(cutoffs).__name__}"
            )
        validated: list[int] = []
        previous: int | None = None
        for position, cutoff in enumerate(cutoffs):
            name = f"cutoffs[{position}]"
            if isinstance(cutoff, bool) or not isinstance(cutoff, int):
                raise TypeError(
                    f"{name} must be an int, got {type(cutoff).__name__}"
                )
            if cutoff < 0:
                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be non-negative")
            if previous is not None and cutoff <= previous:
                raise ValueError(
                    "cutoffs must be strictly increasing"
                )
            previous = cutoff
            validated.append(cutoff)
        return tuple(validated)

    @staticmethod
    def _empty_backtest_totals() -> dict[str, int]:
        """Return a fresh zeroed six-counter backtest totals dict."""
        return {
            "predictions": 0,
            "hit": 0,
            "early": 0,
            "late": 0,
            "missed": 0,
            "unresolved": 0,
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _build_lifetime_churn_backtest_cutoff(
        cutoff: int,
        forecast_records: tuple[dict[str, object], ...],
        members_by_wave: list[set[tuple[str, object]]],
        last_wave: int,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Score one cutoff's forecasts against the later observed waves.

        Used only by :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_backtests`. The
        forecast records are already the complete, periodicity-sorted
        result of :meth:`_build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result` for the
        cutoff's prefix wave set, and ``members_by_wave`` is the frozen
        view's complete wave membership indexed by serial number. Each
        prediction is scanned from its ``earliest`` bound toward its
        ``latest`` bound -- only observed serials greater than the
        cutoff can match -- and the first wave whose members include the
        identity sets ``actual``: the center wave is ``hit``, a wave
        before it is ``early`` and one after it is ``late``. With no
        match, a fully observed interval (``latest`` at most
        ``last_wave``) is ``missed`` and an interval still open at the
        observation end is ``unresolved``. Outcomes keep the forecast
        record order and ascending ordinal order; every object is built
        fresh and shares nothing with the records or the membership
        sets.
        """
        outcomes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        totals = BranchStore._empty_backtest_totals()
        for record in forecast_records:
            key = (record["type"], record["identity"])
            for prediction in record["forecasts"]:
                predicted = prediction["wave"]
                earliest = max(prediction["earliest"], cutoff + 1)
                latest = prediction["latest"]
                actual = None
                status = None
                upper = min(latest, last_wave)
                for serial in range(earliest, upper + 1):
                    if key in members_by_wave[serial]:
                        actual = serial
                        if serial == predicted:
                            status = "hit"
                        elif serial < predicted:
                            status = "early"
                        else:
                            status = "late"
                        break
                if status is None:
                    status = (
                        "missed" if latest <= last_wave else "unresolved"
                    )
                outcomes.append(
                    {
                        "type": record["type"],
                        "identity": BranchStore._freeze_lifetime_value(
                            record["identity"]
                        ),
                        "ordinal": prediction["ordinal"],
                        "predicted": predicted,
                        "earliest": prediction["earliest"],
                        "latest": latest,
                        "actual": actual,
                        "status": status,
                    }

def lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_backtests(
        self,
        reference: str,
        series: dict[str, tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]],
        base_scenario: dict[str, object],
        axis: str,
        values: tuple[int | float, ...],
        min_size: int,
        max_size: int,
        required: tuple[str, ...],
        exclusive_pairs: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...],
        limit: int,
        windows: tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...],
        causes: tuple[str, ...],
        direction: str,
        depth: int,
        node_limit: int,
        change_limit: int,
        lifetime_limit: int,
        diff_limit: int,
        window_limit: int,
        total_diff_limit: int,
        churn_limit: int,
        streak_limit: int,
        min_identities: int,
        wave_limit: int,
        min_waves: int,
        recurrence_limit: int,
        max_jitter: int,
        periodicity_limit: int,
        horizon: int,
        forecast_limit: int,
        cutoffs: tuple[int, ...],
        backtest_limit: int,
        min_resolved: int,
        scorecard_limit: int,
        split_cutoffs: tuple[int, ...],
        min_rate_drop: tuple[int, int],
        drift_limit: int,
        scan_limit: int,
        min_splits: int,
        streak_result_limit: int,
        min_active_identities: int,
        wave_result_limit: int,
        min_wave_occurrences: int,
        recurrence_result_limit: int,
        max_wave_jitter: int,
        periodicity_result_limit: int,
        wave_horizon: int,
        prediction_result_limit: int,
        wave_cutoffs: tuple[int, ...],
        match_tolerance: int,
        prediction_backtest_limit: int,
        token: str | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Backtest the drift-wave projections against the later waves.

        Reuses every public input, parameter order, validation order,
        stage cap and frozen-view semantic of
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_predictions`,
        appending ``wave_cutoffs``, ``match_tolerance`` and
        ``prediction_backtest_limit`` in that order after
        ``prediction_result_limit`` (still before the split membership
        check and any state lookup), keeping the same optional trailing
        ``token``. ``wave_cutoffs`` must be a tuple of non-``bool``
        :class:`int` values, strictly increasing: a non-tuple container
        or a ``bool``/non-:class:`int` element raises
        :class:`TypeError`, while a negative, duplicate or
        non-strictly-increasing element raises :class:`ValueError`;
        once the drift wave set exists, an element beyond its last wave
        serial also raises :class:`ValueError` (an empty wave set skips
        that range check). ``match_tolerance`` must be a non-``bool``
        non-negative :class:`int` and ``prediction_backtest_limit`` a
        non-``bool`` :class:`int` of at least one (a ``bool`` or
        non-:class:`int` raises :class:`TypeError`, an out-of-range
        value :class:`ValueError`).

        The scan, streak and wave stages run exactly once, exactly as
        in :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_predictions`, and
        the complete drift wave set of the one frozen view is the
        observation set. Each wave cutoff is a drift-wave serial
        number: training at that cutoff reruns the recurrence and
        periodicity stages -- with their own caps and
        ``max_wave_jitter`` -- on the prefix of waves with serial
        numbers at most the cutoff, so an identity takes part only
        with at least three training appearances and a jitter of at
        most ``max_wave_jitter``, and its period, jitter and record
        order come from the prefix alone. Each kept identity then
        projects from its last training wave by its integer period
        exactly as the predictions query does, keeping only projected
        waves within ``wave_horizon`` of that last training wave; an
        identity with no projected wave inside that window returns no
        record. ``prediction_result_limit`` bounds each cutoff's
        record set and ``prediction_backtest_limit`` bounds the
        complete cross-cutoff record set, each checked only once its
        set is complete, so an over-limit query raises
        :class:`ValueError` without truncating.

        A cutoff's evaluation window is the observed waves with serial
        numbers greater than the cutoff and at most ``cutoff +
        wave_horizon``. Each target, in ascending wave order, claims
        the nearest still-unmatched appearance of the same identity
        inside the window whose distance is at most
        ``match_tolerance`` -- equal distances go to the earlier
        observed wave and no observed wave is matched twice -- and is
        ``hit`` with that wave as its ``actual``; an unmatched target
        is ``missed`` when it does not exceed the observation set's
        last wave and ``unresolved`` when it does. Observed
        appearances inside the window that no target claims are the
        record's ``unexpected`` count.

        The result is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered ``backtests,
        totals``. Each record is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
        ``cutoff, identity, period, jitter, last_wave, targets, hit,
        missed, unresolved, unexpected``; ``targets`` is an ascending
        tuple of fresh dicts ordered ``wave, offset, actual, status``,
        with ``actual`` the matched wave's serial or ``None``. Records
        sort by cutoff ascending and then keep the cutoff's
        periodicity order. ``totals`` is a fresh dict with keys
        ordered ``cutoffs, records, hit, missed, unresolved,
        unexpected``: the number of cutoffs represented in the
        records, the record count and the four summed counters. An
        empty ``wave_cutoffs`` tuple, an empty wave set and a query
        with no qualifying identity all return an empty ``backtests``
        tuple and six zero totals. Every object is built fresh and
        shares nothing with internal state; a tokenized success
        consumes exactly one read while any failure refunds it, and a
        tokenless query observes the same frozen view and never
        mutates branches, the event graph or persistence files.
        """
        # Ordinary inputs are validated first, in exactly the existing
        # order, but no branch or historical node is looked up yet.
        validated = self._validate_frontier_inputs(
            reference,
            series,
            base_scenario,
            axis,
            values,
            min_size,
            max_size,
            required,
            exclusive_pairs,
            limit,
        )

        # Every cap is checked exactly as in
        # lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_predictions; wave_cutoffs,
        # match_tolerance and prediction_backtest_limit follow
        # prediction_result_limit in that order, still before the split
        # membership check and every state lookup. Wave cutoffs cannot
        # be range-checked until the actual drift waves are known, so
        # only their types, non-negativity and strict ordering are
        # settled here.
        point_count = self._frontier_point_count(validated)
        index_windows = self._validate_lifetime_windows(windows, point_count)

        causes, direction, depth_value, node_limit_value = (
            self._validate_slice_inputs(causes, direction, depth, node_limit)
        )
        change_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            change_limit, "change_limit"
        )
        lifetime_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            lifetime_limit, "lifetime_limit"
        )
        diff_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            diff_limit, "diff_limit"
        )
        window_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            window_limit, "window_limit"
        )
        total_diff_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            total_diff_limit, "total_diff_limit"
        )
        churn_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            churn_limit, "churn_limit"
        )
        streak_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            streak_limit, "streak_limit"
        )
        min_identities_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            min_identities, "min_identities"
        )
        wave_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            wave_limit, "wave_limit"
        )
        min_waves_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            min_waves, "min_waves"
        )
        recurrence_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            recurrence_limit, "recurrence_limit"
        )
        max_jitter_value = BranchStore._require_non_negative_limit(
            max_jitter, "max_jitter"
        )
        periodicity_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            periodicity_limit, "periodicity_limit"
        )
        horizon_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(horizon, "horizon")
        forecast_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            forecast_limit, "forecast_limit"
        )
        cutoffs_value = BranchStore._validate_backtest_cutoffs(cutoffs)
        backtest_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            backtest_limit, "backtest_limit"
        )
        min_resolved_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            min_resolved, "min_resolved"
        )
        scorecard_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            scorecard_limit, "scorecard_limit"
        )
        split_cutoffs_value = (
            BranchStore._validate_drift_scan_split_cutoffs(split_cutoffs)
        )
        min_rate_drop_value = BranchStore._validate_min_rate_drop(
            min_rate_drop
        )
        drift_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            drift_limit, "drift_limit"
        )
        scan_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            scan_limit, "scan_limit"
        )
        min_splits_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            min_splits, "min_splits"
        )
        streak_result_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            streak_result_limit, "streak_result_limit"
        )
        min_active_identities_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            min_active_identities, "min_active_identities"
        )
        wave_result_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            wave_result_limit, "wave_result_limit"
        )
        min_wave_occurrences_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            min_wave_occurrences, "min_wave_occurrences"
        )
        recurrence_result_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            recurrence_result_limit, "recurrence_result_limit"
        )
        max_wave_jitter_value = BranchStore._require_non_negative_limit(
            max_wave_jitter, "max_wave_jitter"
        )
        periodicity_result_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            periodicity_result_limit, "periodicity_result_limit"
        )
        wave_horizon_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            wave_horizon, "wave_horizon"
        )
        prediction_result_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            prediction_result_limit, "prediction_result_limit"
        )
        wave_cutoffs_value = BranchStore._validate_wave_cutoffs(wave_cutoffs)
        match_tolerance_value = BranchStore._require_non_negative_limit(
            match_tolerance, "match_tolerance"
        )
        prediction_backtest_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            prediction_backtest_limit, "prediction_backtest_limit"
        )
        BranchStore._validate_drift_scan_splits(
            cutoffs_value, split_cutoffs_value
        )
        if len(index_windows) > window_limit_value:
            raise ValueError(
                f"lifetime churn window limit exceeded: "
                f"{len(index_windows)} windows, limit is "
                f"{window_limit_value}"
            )

        # The scan, streak and wave stages run exactly once on one
        # frozen view, exactly as in the predictions query; the
        # complete drift wave set is then the observation set every
        # cutoff's prefix training and later-wave scoring reads from.
        view = self
        if token is not None:
            view = self._reserve_snapshot_read(token)
        try:
            results, _grand_totals = (
                view._compute_lifetime_backtest_cutoffs(
                    validated,
                    index_windows,

def _build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_backtests_result(
        wave_records: tuple[dict[str, object], ...],
        min_wave_occurrences: int,
        recurrence_result_limit: int,
        max_wave_jitter: int,
        periodicity_result_limit: int,
        wave_horizon: int,
        prediction_result_limit: int,
        wave_cutoffs: tuple[int, ...],
        match_tolerance: int,
        prediction_backtest_limit: int,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Score each cutoff's prefix-trained projections on later waves.

        Used only by
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_backtests`.
        The wave records are the complete, already-bounded ``waves``
        tuple of
        :meth:`_build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_waves_result`, so
        each wave's position in the tuple is its zero-based serial
        number and the last serial is the observation end. When the
        wave set is non-empty, every cutoff beyond its last serial
        raises :class:`ValueError` before any training runs; an empty
        wave set skips the range check and scores nothing.

        Each cutoff reruns the recurrence and periodicity aggregations
        on the prefix of waves with serial numbers at most the cutoff,
        with ``min_wave_occurrences``, ``max_wave_jitter`` and the two
        stage caps applied exactly as in the predictions query, and
        then projects each kept identity's waves from its last
        training wave by its median period, keeping only offsets of at
        most ``wave_horizon``. The evaluation window is the observed
        serials greater than the cutoff and at most ``cutoff +
        wave_horizon``; targets claim same-identity appearances in
        that window in ascending target order, nearest first, equal
        distances going to the earlier wave, never reusing an
        appearance. A claimed target is ``hit``; an unclaimed one is
        ``missed`` when it does not exceed the observation end and
        ``unresolved`` when it does; unclaimed window appearances
        count as ``unexpected``.

        ``prediction_result_limit`` bounds each cutoff's complete
        record set and ``prediction_backtest_limit`` the complete
        cross-cutoff set, both enforced only once the set is built, so
        an over-limit query raises :class:`ValueError` without
        truncating. Records sort by cutoff ascending and then keep the
        cutoff's periodicity order; ``totals`` counts the represented
        cutoffs, the records and the four outcome counters. Every
        record, target and totals dict is built fresh and shares no
        mutable object with the wave records.
        """
        last_wave = len(wave_records) - 1
        if wave_records:
            # A cutoff's range is only meaningful once the wave set
            # exists; an empty wave set scores nothing at all.
            for cutoff in wave_cutoffs:
                if cutoff > last_wave:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"wave cutoff {cutoff} is out of range for "
                        f"{last_wave + 1} wave(s)"
                    )

        # Each identity's observed wave serials, ascending, answer
        # every cutoff's matching from the one observation set.
        serials_by_identity: dict[object, list[int]] = {}
        for serial, wave in enumerate(wave_records):
            present: set[object] = set()
            for point in wave["points"]:
                for identity in point["identities"]:
                    present.add(identity)
            for identity in present:
                serials_by_identity.setdefault(identity, []).append(serial)

        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        for cutoff in wave_cutoffs:
            # Training sees only waves with serial numbers at most the
            # cutoff; the recurrence and periodicity stages rerun on
            # that prefix with their own caps, so every record's
            # period, jitter and order come from the prefix alone.
            recurrences = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_recurrences_result(
                wave_records[: cutoff + 1],
                min_wave_occurrences,
                recurrence_result_limit,
            )
            periodicities = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_periodicities_result(
                recurrences["recurrences"],
                max_wave_jitter,
                periodicity_result_limit,
            )
            window_end = cutoff + wave_horizon
            cutoff_records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
            for periodicity in periodicities["periodicities"]:
                identity = periodicity["identity"]
                period = periodicity["period"]
                last_training = periodicity["last_wave"]
                target_waves: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
                offset = period
                while offset <= wave_horizon:
                    target_waves.append((last_training + offset, offset))
                    offset += period
                if not target_waves:
                    continue
                # Observed appearances of the identity after the
                # cutoff and inside the evaluation window, ascending.
                reals = [
                    serial
                    for serial in serials_by_identity.get(identity, ())
                    if cutoff < serial <= window_end
                ]
                used = [False] * len(reals)
                targets: list[dict[str, object]] = []
                hit = 0
                missed = 0
                unresolved = 0
                for target_wave, target_offset in target_waves:
                    best_index: int | None = None
                    best_distance: int | None = None
                    for index, real in enumerate(reals):
                        if used[index]:
                            continue
                        distance = real - target_wave
                        if distance < 0:
                            distance = -distance
                        if distance > match_tolerance:
                            continue
                        # Ascending scan with a strict improvement
                        # test keeps the earlier wave on ties.
                        if best_distance is None or distance < best_distance:
                            best_distance = distance
                            best_index = index
                    if best_index is not None:
                        used[best_index] = True
                        actual: int | None = reals[best_index]
                        status = "hit"
                        hit += 1
                    else:
                        actual = None
                        if target_wave <= last_wave:
                            status = "missed"
                            missed += 1
                        else:
                            status = "unresolved"
                            unresolved += 1
                    targets.append(
                        {
                            "wave": target_wave,
                            "offset": target_offset,
                            "actual": actual,
                            "status": status,
                        }
                    )
                cutoff_records.append(
                    {
                        "cutoff": cutoff,
                        "identity": BranchStore._freeze_lifetime_value(
                            identity
                        ),
                        "period": period,
                        "jitter": periodicity["jitter"],
                        "last_wave": last_training,
                        "targets": tuple(targets),
                        "hit": hit,
                        "missed": missed,
                        "unresolved": unresolved,
                        "unexpected": used.count(False),
                    }
                )
            if len(cutoff_records) > prediction_result_limit:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"lifetime churn drift wave prediction result "
                    f"limit exceeded: {len(cutoff_records)} prediction "
                    f"records, limit is {prediction_result_limit}"
                )
            records.extend(cutoff_records)

        if len(records) > prediction_backtest_limit:
            raise ValueError(
                f"lifetime churn drift wave prediction backtest limit "
                f"exceeded: {len(records)} prediction records across "
                f"{len(wave_cutoffs)} cutoff(s), limit is "
                f"{prediction_backtest_limit}"
            )

        cutoff_seen: set[object] = set()
        totals = {
            "cutoffs": 0,
            "records": 0,
            "hit": 0,
            "missed": 0,
            "unresolved": 0,
            "unexpected": 0,
        }
        for record in records:
            cutoff_seen.add(record["cutoff"])
            totals["records"] += 1
            totals["hit"] += record["hit"]
            totals["missed"] += record["missed"]
            totals["unresolved"] += record["unresolved"]
            totals["unexpected"] += record["unexpected"]
        totals["cutoffs"] = len(cutoff_seen)
        return {"backtests": tuple(records), "totals": totals}

    @staticmethod
    def _lifetime_identity_unicode_key(identity: object) -> tuple:
        """Build a total-order key sorting one identity by code points.

        Drift-wave identities are nested tuples of strings (a node is
        ``(cause, key)``, an edge is two such tuples, and a gap also
        carries an integer interval), so plain tuple comparison cannot
        order the whole set. Strings compare by Unicode code point,
        tuples compare lexicographically over their element keys, and
        the type tags make the key total across types; the tags order
        strings before tuples before integers solely to make every
        comparison defined -- every compared pair of real identities
        shares the same shape.
        """
        if isinstance(identity, str):
            return (0, identity)
        if isinstance(identity, tuple):
            return (
                1,
                tuple(
                    BranchStore._lifetime_identity_unicode_key(element)
                    for element in identity
                ),
            )
        return (2, identity)

def _build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_waves_result(
        streaks: tuple[dict[str, object], ...],
        baseline_splits: tuple[int, ...],
        min_active_regressions: int,
        regression_wave_limit: int,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Group positions where enough kept streaks stay active.

        Used only by
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_waves`.
        The streaks are the complete, already-bounded ``streaks`` tuple
        of
        :meth:`_build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_streaks_result`
        in its final order and ``baseline_splits`` the validated
        requested positions. Each requested position counts the
        distinct identities whose kept streak covers it, listed in that
        streak order, and maximal runs of adjacent requested positions
        reaching ``min_active_regressions`` active identities form the
        waves -- unrequested integer positions do not break adjacency,
        while a requested position below the threshold ends the run.
        ``regression_wave_limit`` bounds the final wave count, raising
        :class:`ValueError` rather than truncating. Every wave and
        point dict is built fresh and shares no mutable object with the
        streak records.
        """
        position_of = {
            split: index for index, split in enumerate(baseline_splits)
        }
        coverage: list[list[object]] = [[] for _ in baseline_splits]
        for streak in streaks:
            identity = streak["identity"]
            start = position_of[streak["start_baseline_cutoffs"]]
            end = position_of[streak["end_baseline_cutoffs"]]
            for index in range(start, end + 1):
                coverage[index].append(identity)

        waves: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        current: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        for index, split in enumerate(baseline_splits):
            identities: list[object] = []
            seen: set[object] = set()
            for identity in coverage[index]:
                if identity in seen:
                    continue
                seen.add(identity)
                identities.append(identity)
            if len(identities) >= min_active_regressions:
                current.append(
                    {
                        "baseline_cutoffs": split,
                        "active_count": len(identities),
                        "identities": tuple(
                            BranchStore._freeze_lifetime_value(identity)
                            for identity in identities
                        ),
                    }
                )
                continue
            if current:
                waves.append(
                    BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_regression_wave(
                        current
                    )
                )
                current = []
        if current:
            waves.append(
                BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_regression_wave(current)
            )

        if len(waves) > regression_wave_limit:
            raise ValueError(
                f"lifetime churn drift wave prediction scorecard "
                f"regression wave limit exceeded: {len(waves)} "
                f"waves, limit is {regression_wave_limit}"
            )

        split_seen: set[object] = set()
        identity_seen: set[object] = set()
        totals = {
            "splits": 0,
            "identities": 0,
            "waves": 0,
            "points": 0,
            "peak_active": 0,
        }
        for wave in waves:
            totals["waves"] += 1
            for point in wave["points"]:
                split_seen.add(point["baseline_cutoffs"])
                totals["points"] += 1
                if point["active_count"] > totals["peak_active"]:
                    totals["peak_active"] = point["active_count"]
                for identity in point["identities"]:
                    identity_seen.add(identity)
        totals["splits"] = len(split_seen)
        totals["identities"] = len(identity_seen)
        return {"waves": tuple(waves), "totals": totals}

    @staticmethod
    def _build_lifetime_churn_regression_wave(
        points: list[dict[str, object]],
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Assemble one maximal active run into a fresh wave dict.

        Used only by
        :meth:`_build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_waves_result`.
        The points are the run's already-built point dicts in requested
        split order; the wave keeps them as one fresh tuple.
        """
        return {
            "start_baseline_cutoffs": points[0]["baseline_cutoffs"],
            "end_baseline_cutoffs": points[-1]["baseline_cutoffs"],
            "split_count": len(points),
            "peak_regressions": max(
                point["active_count"] for point in points
            ),
            "points": tuple(points),
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_recurrences_result(
        waves: tuple[dict[str, object], ...],
        min_regression_wave_occurrences: int,
        regression_wave_recurrence_limit: int,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Aggregate, per identity, the regression waves it recurs in.

        Used only by
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_recurrences`.
        The waves are the complete, already-bounded ``waves`` tuple of
        :meth:`_build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_waves_result`,
        so each wave's position in the tuple is its zero-based wave
        number. An identity listed in a wave's point identities takes
        part in that wave once, however many of the wave's points list
        it; only identities taking part in at least
        ``min_regression_wave_occurrences`` waves keep a record with
        ordered keys ``identity, waves, first_wave, last_wave, span,
        points, peak_active, appearances``. Records sort by
        participating-wave count and summed point count descending,
        then ``first_wave`` ascending, then the identities'
        first-encounter order across the waves. The complete set is
        built before ``regression_wave_recurrence_limit`` is enforced,
        so an over-limit query raises :class:`ValueError` without
        truncating. Every record and appearance dict is built fresh and
        shares no mutable object with the wave records.
        """
        encounter: dict[object, int] = {}
        appearances: dict[object, list[dict[str, object]]] = {}
        peaks: dict[object, int] = {}
        for serial, wave in enumerate(waves):
            per_wave: dict[object, dict[str, object]] = {}
            for point in wave["points"]:
                active_count = point["active_count"]
                for identity in point["identities"]:
                    if identity not in encounter:
                        encounter[identity] = len(encounter)
                    entry = per_wave.get(identity)
                    if entry is None:
                        entry = {
                            "wave": serial,
                            "start_baseline_cutoffs": wave[
                                "start_baseline_cutoffs"
                            ],
                            "end_baseline_cutoffs": wave[
                                "end_baseline_cutoffs"
                            ],
                            "points": 0,
                            "first_baseline_cutoffs": point[
                                "baseline_cutoffs"
                            ],
                            "last_baseline_cutoffs": point[
                                "baseline_cutoffs"
                            ],
                        }
                        per_wave[identity] = entry
                    entry["points"] += 1
                    entry["last_baseline_cutoffs"] = point[
                        "baseline_cutoffs"
                    ]
                    if active_count > peaks.get(identity, 0):
                        peaks[identity] = active_count
            for identity, entry in per_wave.items():
                appearances.setdefault(identity, []).append(entry)

        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        for identity, wave_appearances in appearances.items():
            if len(wave_appearances) < min_regression_wave_occurrences:
                continue
            first_wave = wave_appearances[0]["wave"]
            last_wave = wave_appearances[-1]["wave"]
            records.append(
                {
                    "identity": BranchStore._freeze_lifetime_value(identity),
                    "waves": len(wave_appearances),
                    "first_wave": first_wave,
                    "last_wave": last_wave,
                    "span": last_wave - first_wave + 1,
                    "points": sum(
                        appearance["points"]
                        for appearance in wave_appearances
                    ),
                    "peak_active": peaks[identity],
                    "appearances": tuple(wave_appearances),
                }
            )

        records.sort(
            key=lambda record: (
                -record["waves"],
                -record["points"],
                record["first_wave"],
                encounter[record["identity"]],
            )
        )
        if len(records) > regression_wave_recurrence_limit:
            raise ValueError(
                f"lifetime churn drift wave prediction scorecard "
                f"regression wave recurrence limit exceeded: "
                f"{len(records)} recurrence records, limit is "
                f"{regression_wave_recurrence_limit}"
            )

        totals = {
            "recurrences": 0,
            "waves": 0,
            "points": 0,
            "first_wave": 0,
            "last_wave": 0,
        }
        for record in records:
            totals["recurrences"] += 1
            totals["waves"] += record["waves"]
            totals["points"] += record["points"]
        if records:
            totals["first_wave"] = min(
                record["first_wave"] for record in records
            )
            totals["last_wave"] = max(
                record["last_wave"] for record in records
            )
        return {"recurrences": tuple(records), "totals": totals}

    @staticmethod
    def _build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_periodicities_result(
        recurrence_records: tuple[dict[str, object], ...],
        max_regression_wave_jitter: int,
        regression_wave_periodicity_limit: int,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Keep the recurrences whose regression-wave cadence is steady.

        Used only by
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_periodicities`.
        The records are the complete, already-bounded and
        already-sorted ``recurrences`` tuple of
        :meth:`_build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_recurrences_result`,
        so their order already breaks every participating-wave, point
        and first-wave tie by the identities' first-encounter order
        across the waves. An identity needs at least three
        appearances; the intervals are the differences of consecutive
        participating wave numbers in ascending wave order, and a
        record is kept only when its largest interval minus its
        smallest is at most ``max_regression_wave_jitter``.

        Each kept record reproduces every recurrence field in the same
        order and appends ``intervals, period, jitter``: ``intervals``
        keeps the adjacent-wave gaps in appearance order, ``period``
        is the integer median of the sorted intervals (the smaller of
        the two middle values for an even count) and ``jitter`` is the
        largest interval minus the smallest. Records sort by
        ``jitter`` ascending, then participating-wave count and summed
        point count descending, then ``first_wave`` ascending; the
        sort is stable over the incoming recurrence order, so a full
        tie falls back to the identities' first-encounter order across
        the waves. The complete candidate set is built before
        ``regression_wave_periodicity_limit`` is enforced, so an
        over-limit query raises :class:`ValueError` without
        truncating. Every record and appearance dict is built fresh
        and shares no mutable object with the recurrence records.
        """
        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        for record in recurrence_records:
            wave_appearances = record["appearances"]
            # Three appearances are the minimum that yields two
            # intervals and a meaningful cadence.
            if len(wave_appearances) < 3:
                continue
            intervals = tuple(
                later["wave"] - earlier["wave"]
                for earlier, later in zip(
                    wave_appearances, wave_appearances[1:]
                )
            )
            jitter = max(intervals) - min(intervals)
            if jitter > max_regression_wave_jitter:
                continue
            ordered_intervals = sorted(intervals)
            middle = len(ordered_intervals) // 2
            if len(ordered_intervals) % 2 == 0:
                # An even interval count takes the smaller middle value.
                period = ordered_intervals[middle - 1]
            else:
                period = ordered_intervals[middle]
            records.append(
                {
                    "identity": BranchStore._freeze_lifetime_value(
                        record["identity"]
                    ),
                    "waves": record["waves"],
                    "first_wave": record["first_wave"],
                    "last_wave": record["last_wave"],
                    "span": record["span"],
                    "points": record["points"],
                    "peak_active": record["peak_active"],
                    "appearances": tuple(
                        dict(appearance) for appearance in wave_appearances
                    ),
                    "intervals": intervals,
                    "period": period,
                    "jitter": jitter,
                }
            )

        records.sort(
            key=lambda record: (
                record["jitter"],
                -record["waves"],
                -record["points"],
                record["first_wave"],
            )
        )
        if len(records) > regression_wave_periodicity_limit:
            raise ValueError(
                f"lifetime churn drift wave prediction scorecard "
                f"regression wave periodicity limit exceeded: "
                f"{len(records)} periodicity records, limit is "
                f"{regression_wave_periodicity_limit}"
            )

        totals = {
            "periodicities": 0,
            "waves": 0,
            "points": 0,
            "first_wave": 0,
            "last_wave": 0,
            "mean_period": 0,
        }
        for record in records:
            totals["periodicities"] += 1
            totals["waves"] += record["waves"]
            totals["points"] += record["points"]
        if records:
            totals["first_wave"] = min(
                record["first_wave"] for record in records
            )
            totals["last_wave"] = max(
                record["last_wave"] for record in records
            )
            totals["mean_period"] = (
                sum(record["period"] for record in records) // len(records)
            )
        return {"periodicities": tuple(records), "totals": totals}

def periodicities_kwargs(store_args, **overrides) -> dict:
    max_regression_wave_jitter = overrides.pop(
        "max_regression_wave_jitter", 10
    )
    regression_wave_periodicity_limit = overrides.pop(
        "regression_wave_periodicity_limit", 50
    )
    kwargs = recurrences_kwargs(store_args, **overrides)
    kwargs["max_regression_wave_jitter"] = max_regression_wave_jitter
    kwargs["regression_wave_periodicity_limit"] = (
        regression_wave_periodicity_limit
    )
    return kwargs


def periodicities_call(store, store_args, **overrides):
    return store.lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_periodicities(
        **periodicities_kwargs(store_args, **overrides)
    )


def build_periodicities(
    recurrences,
    max_regression_wave_jitter=10,
    regression_wave_periodicity_limit=50,
):
    return BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_periodicities_result(
        recurrences,
        max_regression_wave_jitter,
        regression_wave_periodicity_limit,
    )


class LifetimeChurnForecastDriftWavePredictionScorecardRegressionWavePeriodicitiesSignatureTests(
    unittest.TestCase
):
    def test_public_signature_appends_two_parameters(self):
        parameters = list(
            inspect.signature(
                BranchStore.lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_periodicities
            ).parameters.values()
        )
        names = [p.name for p in parameters]
        recurrence_names = list(
            inspect.signature(
                BranchStore.lifetime_churn_forecast_drift_wave_prediction_scorecard_regression_wave_recurrences
            ).parameters
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            names,
            recurrence_names[:-1]

                "max_regression_wave_jitter",
                "regression_wave_periodicity_limit",
                "token",
            ],
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            [p.default for p in parameters[:-1]],
            [inspect.Parameter.empty] * (len(parameters) - 1),
        )
        self.assertIsNone(parameters[-1].default)

    def test_result_shape_and_key_order(self):
        waves = (
            make_wave(1, [(1, 1, ("A",))]),
            make_wave(2, [(2, 1, ("A",))]),
            make_wave(3, [(3, 1, ("A",))]),

        recurrences = build_recurrences(waves)
        result = build_periodicities(recurrences["recurrences"])
        self.assertEqual(list(result), ["periodicities", "totals"])
        self.assertIsInstance(result["periodicities"], tuple)
        record = result["periodicities"][0]
        self.assertEqual(
            list(record),
            [
                "identity",
                "waves",
                "first_wave",
                "last_wave",
                "span",
                "points",
                "peak_active",
                "appearances",
                "intervals",
                "period",
                "jitter",
            ],
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            list(record["appearances"][0]),
            [
                "wave",
                "start_baseline_cutoffs",
                "end_baseline_cutoffs",
                "points",
                "first_baseline_cutoffs",
                "last_baseline_cutoffs",
            ],
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            list(result["totals"]),
            [
                "periodicities",
                "waves",
                "points",
                "first_wave",
                "last_wave",
                "mean_period",
            ],
        )


class LifetimeChurnForecastDriftWavePredictionScorecardRegressionWavePeriodicitiesResultTests(
    unittest.TestCase
):
    def test_steady_cadence_record(self):
        waves = (
            make_wave(1, [(1, 2, ("A",))]),
            make_wave(2, [(2, 1, ("A",))]),
            make_wave(3, [(3, 3, ("A",))]),
        )
        recurrences = build_recurrences(waves)
        result = build_periodicities(recurrences["recurrences"])
        self.assertEqual(len(result["periodicities"]), 1)
        record = result["periodicities"][0]
        self.assertEqual(record["identity"], "A")
        self.assertEqual(record["waves"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(record["first_wave"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(record["last_wave"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(record["span"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(record["points"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(record["peak_active"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(record["intervals"], (1, 1))
        self.assertEqual(record["period"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(record["jitter"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(
            result["totals"],
            {
                "periodicities": 1,
                "waves": 3,
                "points": 3,
                "first_wave": 0,
                "last_wave": 2,
                "mean_period": 1,
            },
        )

    def test_two_appearances_never_qualify(self):
        waves = (
            make_wave(1, [(1, 1, ("A",))]),
            make_wave(2, [(2, 1, ("A",))]),
        )
        recurrences = build_recurrences(waves)
        self.assertEqual(len(recurrences["recurrences"]), 1)
        result = build_periodicities(recurrences["recurrences"])
        self.assertEqual(result["periodicities"], ())
        self.assertEqual(
            result["totals"],
            {
                "periodicities": 0,
                "waves": 0,
                "points": 0,
                "first_wave": 0,
                "last_wave": 0,
                "mean_period": 0,
            },
        )

    def test_even_interval_count_takes_the_smaller_middle_period(self):
        waves = (
            make_wave(1, [(1, 1, ("A",))]),
            make_wave(2, [(2, 1, ("B",))]),
            make_wave(3, [(3, 1, ("A",))]),
            make_wave(4, [(4, 1, ("B",))]),
            make_wave(5, [(5, 1, ("C",))]),
            make_wave(6, [(6, 1, ("C",))]),
            make_wave(7, [(7, 1, ("A",))]),
        )
        # "A" takes part in waves 0, 2 and 6; "B" and "C" never reach
        # three appearances.
        recurrences = build_recurrences(waves)
        result = build_periodicities(recurrences["recurrences"])
        self.assertEqual(len(result["periodicities"]), 1)
        record = result["periodicities"][0]
        self.assertEqual(record["intervals"], (2, 4))
        self.assertEqual(record["period"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(record["jitter"], 2)

    def test_odd_interval_count_takes_the_middle_period(self):
        waves = (
            make_wave(1, [(1, 1, ("A",))]),
            make_wave(2, [(2, 1, ("A",))]),
            make_wave(3, [(3, 1, ("A",))]),
            make_wave(4, [(4, 1, ("B",))]),
            make_wave(5, [(5, 1, ("A",))]),
        )
        # "A" takes part in waves 0, 1, 2 and 4.
        recurrences = build_recurrences(waves)
        result = build_periodicities(recurrences["recurrences"])
        record = result["periodicities"][0]
        self.assertEqual(record["intervals"], (1, 1, 2))
        self.assertEqual(record["period"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(record["jitter"], 1)

    def test_max_regression_wave_jitter_filters_records(self):
        waves = (
            make_wave(1, [(1, 1, ("A", "B"))]),
            make_wave(2, [(2, 1, ("A", "B"))]),
            make_wave(3, [(3, 1, ("A",))]),
            make_wave(4, [(4, 1, ("B",))]),
        )
        # "A" has intervals (1, 1) and jitter 0; "B" has intervals
        # (1, 2) and jitter 1.
        recurrences = build_recurrences(waves)
        result = build_periodicities(
            recurrences["recurrences"], max_regression_wave_jitter=0
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            [record["identity"] for record in result["periodicities"]],
            ["A"],
        )
        result = build_periodicities(
            recurrences["recurrences"], max_regression_wave_jitter=1
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            [record["identity"] for record in result["periodicities"]],
            ["A", "B"],
        )

    def test_records_sort_by_jitter_waves_points_first_wave_then_encounter(
        self,
    ):
        waves = (
            make_wave(1, [(1, 1, ("c", "b", "a", "d"))]),
            make_wave(2, [(2, 1, ("a", "c", "d")), (3, 1, ("a",))]),
            make_wave(3, [(3, 1, ("a", "b", "d"))]),
            make_wave(4, [(4, 1, ("c", "d"))]),
            make_wave(5, [(5, 1, ("b",))]),
        )
        # "a": waves 0-2, intervals (1, 1), jitter 0, four points.
        # "d": waves 0-3, intervals (1, 1, 1), jitter 0, four points.
        # "b": waves 0, 2, 4, intervals (2, 2), jitter 0, three points.
        # "c": waves 0, 1, 3, intervals (1, 2), jitter 1.
        recurrences = build_recurrences(waves)
        result = build_periodicities(recurrences["recurrences"])
        # Jitter 0 first; within it waves descending ("d" has four),
        # then points descending ("a" has four, "b" three). A full tie
        # would fall back to first-encounter order across the waves.
        self.assertEqual(
            [record["identity"] for record in result["periodicities"]],
            ["d", "a", "b", "c"],
        )
        # A full tie falls back to first-encounter order.
        waves = (
            make_wave(1, [(1, 1, ("c", "a"))]),
            make_wave(2, [(2, 1, ("c", "a"))]),
            make_wave(3, [(3, 1, ("c", "a"))]),
        )
        recurrences = build_recurrences(waves)
        result = build_periodicities(recurrences["recurrences"])
        self.assertEqual(
            [record["identity"] for record in result["periodicities"]],
            ["c", "a"],
        )

    def test_regression_wave_periodicity_limit_bounds_the_complete_set(
        self,
    ):
        waves = (
            make_wave(1, [(1, 1, ("A", "B"))]),
            make_wave(2, [(2, 1, ("A", "B"))]),
            make_wave(3, [(3, 1, ("A", "B"))]),
        )
        recurrences = build_recurrences(waves)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
            build_periodicities(
                recurrences["recurrences"], 10, 1
            )
        self.assertIn(
            "regression wave periodicity limit", str(caught.exception)
        )
        result = build_periodicities(recurrences["recurrences"], 10, 2)
        self.assertEqual(len(result["periodicities"]), 2)

    def test_mean_period_is_the_floored_average(self):
        waves = (
            make_wave(1, [(1, 1, ("A", "B"))]),
            make_wave(2, [(2, 1, ("A",))]),
            make_wave(3, [(3, 1, ("A", "B"))]),
            make_wave(4, [(4, 1, ("C",))]),
            make_wave(5, [(5, 1, ("B",))]),
        )
        # "A" takes part in waves 0-2 with period 1; "B" takes part in
        # waves 0, 2 and 4 with intervals (2, 2) and period 2, so the
        # floored mean of (1, 2) is 1.
        recurrences = build_recurrences(waves)
        result = build_periodicities(recurrences["recurrences"])
        self.assertEqual(result["totals"]["mean_period"], 1)

    def test_empty_recurrences_return_empty_tuple_and_zero_totals(self):
        result = build_periodicities(())
        self.assertEqual(result["periodicities"], ())
        self.assertEqual(
            result["totals"],
            {
                "periodicities": 0,
                "waves": 0,
                "points": 0,
                "first_wave": 0,
                "last_wave": 0,
                "mean_period": 0,
            },
        )

    def test_every_object_is_fresh(self):
        waves = (
            make_wave(1, [(1, 1, (("A", "x"),))]),
            make_wave(2, [(2, 1, (("A", "x"),))]),
            make_wave(3, [(3, 1, (("A", "x"),))]),
        )
        recurrences = build_recurrences(waves)
        result = build_periodicities(recurrences["recurrences"])
        result["periodicities"][0]["waves"] = 999
        result["periodicities"][0]["appearances"][0]["points"] = 999
        result["totals"]["periodicities"] = 999
        again = build_periodicities(recurrences["recurrences"])
        self.assertEqual(again["periodicities"][0]["waves"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(
            again["periodicities"][0]["appearances"][0]["points"], 1
        )
        self.assertEqual(again["totals"]["periodicities"], 1)
        # The recurrence records are not mutated either.
        self.assertEqual(recurrences["recurrences"][0]["waves"], 3)

        seen_ids = []

        def collect(value):
            if isinstance(value, dict):
                seen_ids.append(id(value))
                for item in value.values():
                    collect(item)
            elif isinstance(value, (tuple, list)):
                for item in value:
                    collect(item)

        collect(again)
        self.assertEqual(len(seen_ids), len(set(seen_ids)))

class LifetimeChurnForecastDriftWavePredictionScorecardRegressionWavePeriodicitiesValidationTests(
    unittest.TestCase
):
    def setUp(self):
        self.store, self.args = diamond_store()

    def call(self, **overrides):
        return periodicities_call(self.store, self.args, **overrides)

    def extended(self, **overrides):
        overrides.setdefault("split_cutoffs", (4,))
        merged = dict(LONG_ARGS)
        merged.update(overrides)
        return self.call(**merged)

    def test_max_regression_wave_jitter_must_be_a_non_bool_non_negative_int(
        self,
    ):
        for bad in (True, False, 1.0, "1", None, (1,)):
            with self.subTest(value=bad):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    self.extended(max_regression_wave_jitter=bad)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.extended(max_regression_wave_jitter=-1)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.extended(max_regression_wave_jitter=-3)
        # Zero is allowed.
        self.extended(max_regression_wave_jitter=0)

    def test_regression_wave_periodicity_limit_must_be_a_non_bool_positive_int(
        self,
    ):
        for bad in (True, False, 1.0, "1", None, (1,)):
            with self.subTest(value=bad):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    self.extended(regression_wave_periodicity_limit=bad)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.extended(regression_wave_periodicity_limit=0)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.extended(regression_wave_periodicity_limit=-3)

    def test_new_parameters_validated_in_signature_order(self):
        # regression_wave_recurrence_limit fails before
        # max_regression_wave_jitter.
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.extended(
                regression_wave_recurrence_limit="x",
                max_regression_wave_jitter="x",
            )
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.extended(
                regression_wave_recurrence_limit=0,
                max_regression_wave_jitter=-1,
            )
        # max_regression_wave_jitter fails before
        # regression_wave_periodicity_limit.
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.extended(
                max_regression_wave_jitter="x",
                regression_wave_periodicity_limit="x",
            )
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.extended(
                max_regression_wave_jitter=-1,
                regression_wave_periodicity_limit=0,
            )
        # All pass before the split membership check fires.
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.extended(
                split_cutoffs=(99,),
                baseline_splits=(1,),
                min_evaluated_delta=0,
                min_hit_rate_drop=(0, 1),
                regression_limit=1,
                min_consecutive_splits=1,
                regression_streak_limit=1,
                min_active_regressions=1,
                regression_wave_limit=1,
                min_regression_wave_occurrences=1,
                regression_wave_recurrence_limit=1,
                max_regression_wave_jitter=0,
                regression_wave_periodicity_limit=1,
            )

    def test_all_parameter_checks_precede_state_lookups(self):
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.call(
                reference="ghost",
                cutoffs=(0, 1),
                max_regression_wave_jitter="x",
            )
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.call(
                reference="ghost",
                cutoffs=(0, 1),
                max_regression_wave_jitter=-1,
            )
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.call(
                reference="ghost",
                cutoffs=(0, 1),
                regression_wave_periodicity_limit="x",
            )
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.call(
                reference="ghost",
                cutoffs=(0, 1),
                regression_wave_periodicity_limit=0,
            )

    def test_underlying_stage_limits_and_errors_are_unchanged(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
            self.extended(
                wave_cutoffs=(9,),
                baseline_splits=(1,),
                min_evaluated_delta=0,
                min_hit_rate_drop=(0, 1),
                regression_limit=50,
                min_consecutive_splits=1,
                regression_streak_limit=50,
                min_active_regressions=1,
                regression_wave_limit=50,
                min_regression_wave_occurrences=1,
                regression_wave_recurrence_limit=50,
                max_regression_wave_jitter=10,
                regression_wave_periodicity_limit=50,
            )
        self.assertIn("out of range", str(caught.exception))
